rules.rule: Review against WCA style guide §4 Database and migrations. Check: migrations are reversible or declare explicit up/down; indexes are added for new foreign keys and for columns that will be queried, declared inside create_table or via index: true rather than as separate statements; boolean columns use an is_ / has_ prefix and match the conventions of sibling tables; new columns are placed with after:; data backfills are wrapped in up_only; state machines with a natural order use an integer-backed enum; no arbitrary limit: on strings; the schema.rb version matches the migration being added; one-off data fixes belong in lib/tasks, not in a migration (§3.9). ALWAYS ALSO APPLY THESE, they hold for every file: §1.2 inline single-use helpers, but extract the moment a snippet appears a second time; §1.3 prefer immutable operations, in-place mutation is a defect unless a comment justifies it; §1.4 no magic values -- every literal that is not self-evidently meaningful gets a named constant, including durations and thresholds; §1.5 comments explain why, not what; §1.6 do not paper over errors with defensive rescues or null-guards, and do not swallow failed writes; §1.7 reuse an existing helper before writing a new one; §2 naming -- names describe what a value means rather than how it was computed, the shape must match the name, use established WCA vocabulary, and stay internally consistent within the file. Report EVERY occurrence of a violation separately, including repeats of the same rule later in the file -- do not stop after the first instance. Cite the section you are applying and explain in prose why the line violates it. Do NOT propose replacement code: leave the suggestion_code and existing_code fields empty and never emit a ```suggestion block. The author decides how to fix it; your job is to point at the rule. Do NOT report bugs, architecture opinions, missing tests, or anything RuboCop / ESLint / Prettier already enforces. Silence is the correct outcome for a clean file.

Review against WCA style guide §5 API design and §3.8 Controllers. Check: the OpenAPI YAML under next-frontend/openapi/ stays the source of truth and is updated alongside shape changes; field naming is consistent across a schema family; shared fields move up into the base schema; variants use a discriminator on a single enum rather than a bag of mutually-dependent booleans; a field omitted from required is already nullable; nothing is serialized "just in case"; arrays are returned as arrays rather than joined strings; the endpoint returns the same shape regardless of caller; errors carry a specific body via the shared rescue_from machinery; after a mutation the changed entity is returned, not the whole collection; serialization goes through the model's *_SERIALIZE_OPTIONS constants. Guard clauses belong in before_action. Also §3.2 query performance in the response path and §3.4 unchecked update/save return values. Review against WCA style guide §3.8 Controllers. Check: controllers stay thin and push logic into models; guard clauses live in before_action declared immediately above the action they protect; strong params are explicit and prefer params.expect (§3.1); authorization uses the existing can_*? helpers on User rather than hand-rolled role checks; errors go through rescue_from rather than a per-controller shape; serialization uses the model's *_SERIALIZE_OPTIONS constants. Also §3.2 query performance (no query inside a loop, size over count, to_a defeats includes) and §3.4 unchecked update/save return values. Review against WCA style guide §3.9 Jobs and rake tasks. Check: the class name ends in Job and does not start with Run; any new cronjob is registered in JobUtils::WCA_CRONJOBS; ActiveJob already serializes AR models, so do not pass redundant fields the job can look up itself; the primary entity comes first in the argument list; the job is idempotent and safe to retry; one-off data fixes belong in lib/tasks instead. Also §3.2 query performance -- a query inside the loop such as a per-row exists? or find is rejected, hoist it out and pluck the ids once or preload with includes; §3.4 update / create / save / update_columns return a boolean and fail silently -- EVERY such call must either use the bang form or have its return value checked. This includes calls after the loop has finished and calls on a different object than the one being iterated, so a method with two unchecked writes gets two separate comments. Never send mail before confirming the write succeeded; §2.5 Ruby naming -- predicates end in ? and drop should_ / is_ prefixes, mutating or raising methods end in !. Review against WCA style guide §3 Ruby and Rails. §3.1 reach for the Rails idiom -- dig, Array.wrap, index_by / group_by / transform_values, filter_map, create_or_find_by, delegate, column? over unless x.nil?, and current_time_from_proper_timezone rather than Time.now inside a model; belongs_to already implies presence. §3.2 query performance -- never query inside a loop, default to size over count and length, to_a defeats includes, pluck / ids when you only need identifiers, find_each for large batches, counter caches over nested COUNT subqueries. §3.3 prefer declared associations and scopes over hand-rolled where chains, put ordering in the association scope, add distinct when joining through a many-to-many. §3.4 update / create / save / update_columns fail silently -- check the result or use the bang form. §3.5 delete_all skips callbacks and dependent: options, destroy_all does not; choose deliberately and prefer dependent: on the has_many side. §3.6 polymorphism over is_a? type checks. §3.7 multiple dependent writes belong in a transaction. This is the LEGACY frontend. Review against WCA style guide §8. CRITICAL: React Compiler is NOT enabled here, so useCallback and useMemo are REQUIRED to keep references stable and must never be flagged as redundant -- that rule applies only to next-frontend/. Check: Semantic UI dot-notation (Table.Header) over a pile of imports; our own hooks useInputState / useInputUpdater / useLoadedData are used where they fit; fetchJsonOrError is used as-is and not wrapped; URLs are built with the helpers in lib/requests/routes.js.erb rather than string concatenation; mutationFn does not close over component state; useMutation uses onError rather than hand-rolled error handling; watch for onSuccess argument shadowing such as onSuccess={setSuccess}; user-facing errors use Message components; loading states use early returns; <Ref> is used for SemUI components that do not forward refs. Also §10 -- every user-facing string goes through i18n. This is the NEXT.JS frontend. Review against WCA style guide §6 and §7. CRITICAL: React Compiler IS enabled here, so useMemo, useCallback and React.memo are redundant and should be flagged for removal (§6.3) -- the opposite rule applies in app/webpacker/. §6.1 server components by default; add 'use client' only for genuinely interactive widgets and extract just that widget rather than marking a whole page. §6.2 types are derived from the generated OpenAPI types with Pick / Partial / Omit, never hand-declared; no as casts; no ! non-null assertions; prefer undefined over null; use library-provided types. §6.4 Tanstack Query -- spread api.queryOptions rather than nesting useQuery, no enabled: false to freeze a query, let the query client hold state via setQueryData updater functions, isPending is initial fetch only. §6.5 nothing complex inside JSX, prefer children over a string-or-node prop, useEffect is only for syncing with systems outside React and must return cleanup, Luxon DateTime over JS Date, parse dates before sorting. §7 styling -- no style={{}}, no hex colours or arbitrary numbers, use theme tokens, textStyle and recipe variants, and use the Chakra component that already exists rather than hand-rolling layout. Also §10 -- every user-facing string goes through i18n.
